transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-03 14:30 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Marisol Ortega (Elysian CISO), Dr. Henry Lin, Priya Menon

[00:00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, good afternoon. This is Avery from Redwood, thanks for taking the time. Um, quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Marisol: Marisol here, CISO, and I have Priya and Henry with me.
[00:00:11] Priya: Hi, Priya, engineering.
[00:00:13] Henry: Henry, VP clinical.
[00:00:15] Diego: Diego Ramos, solutions eng, Redwood.
[00:00:18] Avery: Great. Agenda - Marisol said you wanted to focus on data governance and specifically the 'no training' commitment and PII handling, is that right?
[00:00:27] Marisol: Yeah, exactly. We're evaluating whether Redwood's hosted or dedicated options meet our regulatory needs. Two big asks: 1) no customer data used for model training and 2) ability to keep PHI out of persistent logs and traces.
[00:00:40] Avery: Totally. We'll run through SOC 2 posture first, then the operational mechanisms - RBAC, SSO, audit logs, KMS - and finally the low-level bits on prompt retention and pilot options.
[00:00:49] Henry: Also data residency - some of our datasets must remain in the EU data center.
[00:00:52] Diego: Yep noted, we'll call out region routing and dedicated capacity placement.
[00:05:12] Diego: Quick note on SOC 2 - Redwood has a Type II report that covers infrastructure, change management, and access controls. We can share a summary and a controls mapping doc. The full report is available under NDA.
[00:05:27] Marisol: Do you have ISO 27001 as well?
[00:05:30] Avery: We're in the process of certifying, we have mapped many controls and have an ISO readiness pack. We can share the mapping.
[00:10:03] Priya: On the auth side, what's your recommendation for SSO? We use SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:10:10] Diego: We support SAML SSO out of the box and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC roles are configurable per account - admin, developer, reader - and you can scope keys to routes. There is also token-level audit trails.
[00:15:00] Marisol: Audit logs - important. We need immutable logs for access and request metadata for three years for our compliance. Can you store logs that long and provide export?
[00:15:10] Diego: We store request logs and admin activity. Retention is configurable per-account for hosted customers; for Dedicated you can choose longer retention and ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding - syslog/S3. Exports are possible.
[00:20:10] Henry: Encryption - BYOK? We want customer-managed keys for PHI datasets.
[00:20:15] Diego: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we offer KMS integrations. You can bring your own keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault, and you can require HSM-backed keys for certain workloads. Keys are never exported to vendor logs.
[00:25:45] Priya: Now, the meat - prompt/content retention. We need guarantees that prompts containing PHI are not used to train models, and ideally they're purged after X hours. What are the defaults and can you opt out entirely?
[00:25:58] Avery: The default for hosted is short-term telemetry for quality and safety; we provide a 'no training' toggle for enterprise accounts. For Dedicated/Private you can disable telemetry and request zero retention beyond ephemeral caching needed for inference. We can provide contractual language to that effect.
[00:30:00] Diego: Implementation detail - there are three layers: 1) runtime KV cache for speed (ephemeral), 2) short-term logs for observability (configurable), 3) long-term analytics or training datasets (only with consent). For the pilot we'd disable layer 3 and set layer 2 retention to minimal or forward logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[00:30:20] Priya: About redaction - do you offer built-in PII/PHI redaction or do we need to pre-process client-side?
[00:30:27] Diego: We have server-side redaction hooks and a pre-built regex/ML redactor you can enable, but for max control we recommend pre-processing on your side in a private VPC before sending. For Dedicated we can help wire a pre-processing step in the request path.
[00:36:12] Henry: A practical question - if a clinician accidentally sends PHI in a prompt, what's the pattern? Can we revoke that content?
[00:36:20] Avery: We can remove entries from logs and scrub traces, but note inference caching and streaming transients might still have short-lived copies. For Dedicated we can guarantee no long-term storage; for hosted we recommend the no-training toggle and per-account retention policies.
[00:36:35] Marisol: And confirm again - no training on our data unless we explicitly opt in?
[00:36:40] Diego: Confirmed. By default we don't incorporate customer content into model training for enterprise accounts without explicit opt-in. We'll provide a written attestation.
[00:40:00] Priya: Is there an encryption-in-transit guarantee for model-to-model or internal control messages?
[00:40:06] Diego: All internal and external traffic is TLS 1.2+, mTLS for service-to-service, and traffic between regions is encrypted.
[00:45:20] Marisol: Data residency - we need compute and logs to live in eu-west and not cross over for certain tenants.
[00:45:27] Avery: For Dedicated we can pin capacity to the EU region and route all requests and logs through EU endpoints. For Hosted we have EU regions and can set routing policies; we'll provide a diagram in the follow-up.
[00:50:00] Diego: As far as auditability, we provide admin activity logs, token usage, model invocation metadata, and an exportable CSV/JSON. For high-security accounts we can also offer a read-only audit view for your auditors via SAML-authenticated access.
[00:55:00] Avery: Quick recap and next steps - we'll: share SOC 2/ISO docs and controls mapping; Diego will set up the sandbox for the redaction pilot on dedicated capacity; Marisol will provide sample prompts and PHI examples; legal teams exchange the no-training clause draft.
